# intellibrix: full API reference

Generated from TSDoc. Index: https://intellibrix.dev/llms.txt

## @intellibrix/agent-tools

### Function agentTools

```ts
agentTools(options: AgentToolsOptions): ToolDefinition[]
```

`apply_patch`, `run_checks`, `todo`, `calculator`, `datetime`, `json_query` and `diff` for a
workspace rooted at `root`, plus `fetch_url`, `web_search`, `memory`, `ask_user` and `delegate`
when you configure them.

### Type Alias AgentToolsOptions

```ts
AgentToolsOptions:
```

### Type Alias ApplyPatchOptions

```ts
ApplyPatchOptions:
```

### Function applyPatchTool

```ts
applyPatchTool(options: ApplyPatchOptions): ToolDefinition
```

An `apply_patch` tool that applies a unified diff to files inside the workspace, atomically:
every hunk of every file is applied in memory first, and nothing is written unless all of them
apply. Line numbers in hunk headers are treated as hints (models get them wrong), so each hunk
is located by its context. Pass `check: true` to validate without writing.

### Function askUserTool

```ts
askUserTool(__namedParameters: AskUserToolOptions): ToolDefinition
```

An `ask_user` tool: the model pauses to ask the human a clarifying question instead of guessing.
The host decides how the question is shown and answered. The answer is the human's own words, so
it is trusted.

### Type Alias AskUserToolOptions

```ts
AskUserToolOptions:
```

### Function braveSearch

```ts
braveSearch(options: SearchProviderOptions & { apiKey: string }): SearchProvider
```

[Brave Search](https://brave.com/search/api/). Needs an API key.

### Function calculatorTool

```ts
calculatorTool(): ToolDefinition
```

A `calculator` tool for exact arithmetic, which models do badly in their heads. It evaluates an
expression with a small parser (no `eval`), so it is safe to run without approval.

### Type Alias CheckFailure

```ts
CheckFailure:
```

One problem pulled out of a check's output.

### Type Alias CheckResult

```ts
CheckResult:
```

The outcome of one named check.

### Type Alias CheckSpec

```ts
CheckSpec:
```

A command the model may run through `run_checks`.

### Function createUnifiedDiff

```ts
createUnifiedDiff(before: string, after: string, options: { afterName?: string; beforeName?: string; context?: number }): UnifiedDiff
```

A unified diff from `before` to `after`, with `context` lines around each change. The output
applies with `patch -p1` or `apply_patch`; a missing final newline is marked the usual way.

### Function datetimeTool

```ts
datetimeTool(options: DatetimeToolOptions): ToolDefinition
```

A `datetime` tool for the things models get wrong: what time it is now, converting between time
zones, adding to a date, and the distance between two dates. Works on ISO 8601 text and IANA time
zone names, with no dependencies.

### Type Alias DatetimeToolOptions

```ts
DatetimeToolOptions:
```

### Type Alias Delegate

```ts
Delegate:
```

Anything that answers a prompt: an `Intelligence`, a `Brick`, or your own wrapper.

### Function delegateTool

```ts
delegateTool(options: DelegateToolOptions): ToolDefinition
```

A `delegate` tool: the model hands a self-contained task to a named sub-agent and gets back its
final answer. The sub-agent keeps its own conversation, tools and approval policy, so configure
`onToolApproval` on its `Intelligence`; delegation never widens what a tool call is allowed to
do. Do not give the sub-agent this tool, or it can delegate to itself without limit.

### Type Alias DelegateToolOptions

```ts
DelegateToolOptions:
```

### Function detectChecks

```ts
detectChecks(root: string): Promise<Record<string, CheckSpec>>
```

Infers checks from `package.json` scripts: `test`, `typecheck` (or `type-check`/`tsc`), `lint`
and `build`, run with the package manager that owns the lockfile. Returns `{}` when there is no
`package.json`.

### Function diffTool

```ts
diffTool(options: DiffToolOptions): ToolDefinition
```

A `diff` tool that compares two files in the workspace, or two pieces of text, and returns a
unified diff: for "what changed between these two versions?" when git has no answer, such as
a generated file against its backup, or a file against the text the model plans to write.

### Type Alias DiffToolOptions

```ts
DiffToolOptions:
```

### Function evaluate

```ts
evaluate(expression: string): number
```

Evaluates an arithmetic expression with a small recursive-descent parser, never `eval`.
Supports `+ - * / % ^ **`, parentheses, the constants `pi`, `e` and `tau`, and common functions
such as `sqrt`, `round`, `min`, `max`, `log` and `sin`. Numbers are IEEE 754 doubles.

### Type Alias FailureParser

```ts
FailureParser: (output: string) => CheckFailure[]
```

Turns a check's (color-stripped) output into structured failures.

### Class FetchBlockedError

```ts
FetchBlockedError
```

- `constructor(message: string): FetchBlockedError`
- `cause`
- `message`
- `name`
- `stack`
- `stackTraceLimit`: The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or `Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).
- `captureStackTrace(targetObject: object, constructorOpt?: Function): void`: Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns a string representing the location in the code at which `Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.
- `prepareStackTrace(err: Error, stackTraces: CallSite[]): any`

### Function fetchUrlTool

```ts
fetchUrlTool(options: FetchUrlToolOptions): ToolDefinition
```

A `fetch_url` tool that reads a web page or API response as text, built so a prompt-injected
model cannot use it to reach your internal network:

- only `http` and `https`;
- the address is checked when the connection is made, so DNS rebinding cannot swap in an internal
  one, and loopback, private, link-local (cloud metadata) and multicast ranges are refused;
- every redirect is followed by hand and re-checked, including against `allowHosts`;
- bounded in size and time, uncompressed, text content types only.

Pages are returned as Markdown of their main content (`format: 'text'` for plain text of the whole
page, `'raw'` for the source) and tagged `untrusted`.
Fetches need approval unless you pin `allowHosts`, because a URL can carry data out in its query
string.

### Type Alias FetchUrlToolOptions

```ts
FetchUrlToolOptions:
```

### Function htmlToMarkdown

```ts
htmlToMarkdown(html: string, options: MarkdownOptions): string
```

Converts an HTML page to Markdown, keeping headings, links, lists, code blocks and tables, and
dropping scripts, navigation, ads, cookie banners and other page furniture. Only the main
content (`<article>` or `<main>`) is kept unless `wholePage` is set.

### Function htmlToText

```ts
htmlToText(html: string): { text: string; title?: string }
```

A readable plain-text rendering of an HTML page: no scripts, styles or markup.

### Function isPrivateAddress

```ts
isPrivateAddress(address: string): boolean
```

Whether `address` is loopback, private, link-local, multicast or otherwise not a public
internet address, including IPv6 forms that wrap an IPv4 address. Anything that is not an IP
literal counts as private so a caller can never fail open.

### Function jsonQueryTool

```ts
jsonQueryTool(options: JsonQueryToolOptions): ToolDefinition
```

A `json_query` tool: run a jq-style query over a JSON (or JSON Lines) file in the workspace so the
model reads only the slice it needs, not a megabyte of API output. Reads only, inside the
workspace jail; results are tagged `untrusted` like any file content.

### Type Alias JsonQueryToolOptions

```ts
JsonQueryToolOptions:
```

### Function memoryTool

```ts
memoryTool(options: MemoryToolOptions): ToolDefinition
```

A `memory` tool: the model saves short notes under a key and finds them again later, even in a
new run, because they live in a `KeyValueStore` you choose. Actions: `save`, `get`, `search`
(keyword match over keys and notes, best first), `list` and `delete`.

Notes come back tagged `untrusted`: the model may have written them after reading a web page, and
a later run must not treat them as instructions. Set `approveChanges` if a human should vet what
gets remembered.

### Type Alias MemoryToolOptions

```ts
MemoryToolOptions:
```

### Function parseRobots

```ts
parseRobots(text: string): Robots
```

### Function parseUnifiedDiff

```ts
parseUnifiedDiff(patch: string): FilePatch[]
```

Parses a unified diff, tolerating `diff --git` headers and wrong hunk line counts.

### Type Alias PatchedFile

```ts
PatchedFile:
```

What a patch did (or would do) to one file.

### Function queryJson

```ts
queryJson(data: unknown, query: string): unknown[]
```

Runs the jq-style `query` over `data` and returns every value it produces.

### Type Alias Robots

```ts
Robots: Group[]
```

A parsed `robots.txt`, as RFC 9309 describes it.

### Function robotsAllows

```ts
robotsAllows(robots: Robots, userAgent: string, path: string): boolean
```

Whether `userAgent` may fetch `path` (path plus query). The most specific user-agent group wins,
then the longest matching rule, with Allow winning a tie.

### Type Alias RunChecksOptions

```ts
RunChecksOptions:
```

### Function runChecksTool

```ts
runChecksTool(options: RunChecksOptions): ToolDefinition
```

A `run_checks` tool that runs named, developer-defined commands (tests, typecheck, lint, build)
and returns structured results (pass/fail, exit code, parsed file/line failures) instead of raw
terminal output, so a model can drive an edit, check, fix loop. The model picks check names,
never command lines. Commands run via `execFile`, never through a shell.

### Interface SearchProvider

```ts
SearchProvider
```

A web-search backend (Brave, Tavily, SearXNG, ...). Implementations are thin; the package
ships no default so you pick one explicitly.

- `id`
- `search(query: string, options: { limit: number; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<SearchResult[]>`

### Type Alias SearchProviderOptions

```ts
SearchProviderOptions:
```

### Type Alias SearchResult

```ts
SearchResult:
```

One hit from a search backend.

### Function searxngSearch

```ts
searxngSearch(options: SearchProviderOptions & { baseUrl: string }): SearchProvider
```

A self-hosted [SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org) instance, which must have the `json` format enabled.

### Function tavilySearch

```ts
tavilySearch(options: SearchProviderOptions & { apiKey: string }): SearchProvider
```

[Tavily](https://tavily.com). Needs an API key.

### Type Alias TodoItem

```ts
TodoItem:
```

### Type Alias TodoStatus

```ts
TodoStatus: "pending" | "in_progress" | "completed"
```

### Class TodoStore

```ts
TodoStore
```

Holds each run's task list so the host can show or persist it.

- `constructor(onChange?: (runId: string, todos: TodoItem[]) => void): TodoStore`
- `clear(runId: string): void`
- `get(runId: string): TodoItem[]`: The task list for `runId` (empty if the model has not made one).
- `set(runId: string, todos: TodoItem[]): void`

### Function todoTool

```ts
todoTool(options: TodoToolOptions): TodoTool
```

A `todo` tool: the model keeps a task list for the current run, replacing the whole list on each
call (omit `todos` to read it back). Lists are scoped to the `runId`. At most one task may be
`in_progress`, which keeps the model working through the list one item at a time.

### Type Alias TodoTool

```ts
TodoTool: ToolDefinition & { store: TodoStore }
```

The `todo` tool plus the `TodoStore` that backs it.

### Type Alias TodoToolOptions

```ts
TodoToolOptions:
```

### Type Alias UnifiedDiff

```ts
UnifiedDiff:
```

### Type Alias UserQuestion

```ts
UserQuestion:
```

A question the model wants a human to answer.

### Function webSearchTool

```ts
webSearchTool(provider: SearchProvider, options: WebSearchToolOptions): ToolDefinition
```

A `web_search` tool over a swappable `SearchProvider`. Results are titles, URLs and
snippets from the open web, so they are tagged `untrusted`; pair it with `fetch_url` to read a
result in full.

### Type Alias WebSearchToolOptions

```ts
WebSearchToolOptions:
```

## @intellibrix/ai-sdk

### Function aiSdkProvider

```ts
aiSdkProvider(model: LanguageModel, opts?: AiSdkProviderOptions): Provider
```

Wraps an AI SDK `LanguageModel` as an intellibrix `Provider`.
`generate`/`stream` each perform exactly one model step (`stepCountIs(1)`)
(tools are declared schema-only via `toAiSdkTools`, with no
`execute` attached), so AI SDK always returns control to `loop.ts` on a
tool-call finish reason instead of looping internally.

### Type Alias AiSdkProviderOptions

```ts
AiSdkProviderOptions:
```

Options for `aiSdkProvider`.

### Function compatibleProvider

```ts
compatibleProvider(model: string, config: { apiKey?: string; baseURL: string; name?: string }, opts?: AiSdkProviderOptions): Provider
```

Resolves an intellibrix `IntellibrixProvider` against an
OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint (Ollama, OpenRouter, vLLM, etc.) via
`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`.

### Function fromAiSdkContent

```ts
fromAiSdkContent(content: ContentPart<ToolSet>[]): Message
```

Converts a single generated step's AI SDK content array into intellibrix's
assistant `Message`.

### Function fromAiSdkFinishReason

```ts
fromAiSdkFinishReason(reason: FinishReason): FinishReason
```

Converts an AI SDK `finishReason` into intellibrix's `FinishReason`.
The two unions are string-for-string identical; this is a type-level
re-tag, not a remapping.

### Function fromAiSdkStep

```ts
fromAiSdkStep(content: ContentPart<ToolSet>[], finishReason: FinishReason, usage: LanguageModelUsage): StepResult
```

Converts a single-step AI SDK `generateText` result's essentials into
intellibrix's `StepResult`.

### Function fromAiSdkUsage

```ts
fromAiSdkUsage(usage: LanguageModelUsage): Usage
```

Converts an AI SDK `LanguageModelUsage` into intellibrix's `Usage`.

### Function provider

```ts
provider(modelString: string, opts?: AiSdkProviderOptions): Provider
```

Resolves an intellibrix `IntellibrixProvider` from a
`"<vendor>:<model>"` string (e.g. `"anthropic:claude-sonnet-5"`), backed by
whichever `@ai-sdk/*` vendor adapter is installed. Throws an actionable
error naming the missing package if the vendor's adapter isn't installed.

### Function toAiSdkMessages

```ts
toAiSdkMessages(messages: Message[]): ModelMessage[]
```

Converts intellibrix's normalized `Message` array into AI SDK's
`ModelMessage[]` shape. `system` messages become AI SDK `system` messages;
`tool` messages become AI SDK `tool` messages carrying tool-result parts.

### Function toAiSdkTools

```ts
toAiSdkTools(tools: ToolDefinition[] | undefined): ToolSet | undefined
```

Converts intellibrix `ToolDefinition[]` into an AI SDK `ToolSet`, declared
schema-only with no `execute` attached, so AI SDK returns control to the
caller on a tool-call finish reason instead of looping internally.

## @intellibrix/cli

### Function init

```ts
init(dir: string, options: InitOptions): Promise<string[]>
```

Scaffolds a new intellibrix project into `dir`. Refuses to write into a
non-empty directory unless `force` is set. Returns the files written.

### Type Alias InitOptions

```ts
InitOptions:
```

### Function loadEntry

```ts
loadEntry(entry: string): Promise<Brick | Structure>
```

Loads a TypeScript (or JS) entry through tsx's programmatic API, in-process,
and returns its default export, which must be a Brick or Structure.

### Function runCli

```ts
runCli(argv: string[]): Promise<McpServerHandle | undefined>
```

Runs the CLI. Returns the live server handle for `mcp serve` so the caller can
close it on shutdown; `undefined` for commands that finish on their own.

### Variable SCAFFOLD_VERSION

```ts
SCAFFOLD_VERSION: "^1.0.0"
```

Version range the scaffolded project depends on.

## @intellibrix/express

### Function askRoute

```ts
askRoute(target: AskTarget): (req: Request, res: Response) => Promise<void>
```

POST handler: reads `{prompt, threadId?}` from the JSON body and replies
`{reply}` with the target's answer. Responds 400 on a missing prompt and 500
on failure.

### Function askStreamRoute

```ts
askStreamRoute(target: AskTarget): (req: Request, res: Response) => Promise<void>
```

GET handler: reads `?prompt=` (and optional `threadId`) and streams the
target's `Intelligence.stream` output as Server-Sent Events, one
`event: <type>` / `data: <json>` frame per stream event. The run is aborted
if the client disconnects.

### Type Alias AskTarget

```ts
AskTarget: Brick | Intelligence
```

Anything `askRoute`/`askStreamRoute` can send a prompt to.

### Class default

```ts
default
```

Class representing a brick that sets up an Express server.
It extends from the `intellibrix!Brick` class.

Access all of Express's functionality through the `ExpressBrick.express` property.

- `constructor(options: ExpressBrickOptions): default`: Creates a new ExpressBrick.
- `ai`: The intelligence of the Brick instance.
- `db`: The key-value store of the Brick instance.
- `events`: The event emitter of the Brick instance.
- `express`: The Express application instance.
- `id`: The unique identifier of the Brick instance.
- `log`: The logger used by the Brick instance.
- `name`: The name of the Brick instance.
- `server`: The HTTP server instance.
- `structure`: The parent Structure of the Brick instance, if any.
- `usage`: Accumulates token usage/cost across every `ask()` call on this Brick.
- `programs`
- `ask(prompt: string, options?: AskOptions): Promise<AskResult>`: Runs a prompt through this Brick's `ai`, offering its programs (via `Brick.tools`) plus any tools attached via `Brick.use`.
- `askEndpoint(path: string, target: AskTarget): default`: Registers `POST <path>` (default `/ask`) answering with `askRoute`.
- `askStreamEndpoint(path: string, target: AskTarget): default`: Registers `GET <path>` (default `/ask/stream`) streaming with `askStreamRoute`.
- `deprogram(name: string): void`: Removes a program from the private map of programs by its name.
- `keepAlive(on: boolean): void`: Toggles the keep alive flag of the Brick instance, which will prevent the Node process from exiting
- `program(program: Program): void`: Adds a program to the private map of programs.
- `run(name: string, payload: any): Promise<any>`: Runs a program by its name with a given payload.
- `schedule(task: Task): Task`: Schedules a `Task` to run on a given schedule.
- `task(name: string): Task | undefined`: Returns a `Task` by its name.
- `tools(): ToolDefinition[]`: Exposes every registered program as a `ToolDefinition`, each `execute` calling `this.run(program.name, input)`.
- `toolset(): ToolDefinition[]`: Every tool this Brick offers: its programs (via `Brick.tools`) plus anything attached via `Brick.use`.
- `unschedule(name: string): void`: Unschedules a task by its name.
- `use(toolsets: ToolDefinition[][]): this`: Attaches external tool arrays (e.g. MCP-sourced tools) to this Brick, included whenever `ask()` builds its tool list.

### Interface ExpressBrickOptions

```ts
ExpressBrickOptions
```

Interface for the options of ExpressBrick.
It extends from `BrickOptions` and adds properties specific to ExpressBrick.

- `builtinMiddleware`: An object specifying whether to use built-in middleware functions.
- `database`: The key-value store of the Brick instance.
- `host`: The host on which the Express server will listen.
- `id`: The unique identifier of the Brick instance.
- `intelligence`: The Intelligence of the Brick instance.
- `logJSON`: A boolean indicating whether the logs should be in JSON format.
- `logLevel`: The log level of the Brick instance.
- `middleware`: An array of middleware functions to use in the Express application.
- `name`: The name of the Brick instance.
- `pinoOptions`: The options for the pino logger used by the Brick instance.
- `port`: The port on which the Express server will listen.
- `routes`: An array of routes that the Express server will handle.
- `structure`: The parent Structure of the Brick, if any.

### Interface ExpressBrickRequest

```ts
ExpressBrickRequest
```

Interface for the request object in ExpressBrick.
It extends from the Request object and adds a property for the Brick instance.

- `aborted`: The `message.aborted` property will be `true` if the request has been aborted.
- `accepted`: Return an array of Accepted media types ordered from highest quality to lowest.
- `app`
- `baseUrl`
- `body`
- `brick`: The Brick instance associated with the request.
- `closed`: Is `true` after `'close'` has been emitted.
- `complete`: The `message.complete` property will be `true` if a complete HTTP message has been received and successfully parsed.
- `connection`: Alias for `message.socket`.
- `cookies`
- `destroyed`: Is `true` after `readable.destroy()` has been called.
- `errored`: Returns error if the stream has been destroyed with an error.
- `fresh`: Check if the request is fresh, aka Last-Modified and/or the ETag still match.
- `headers`: The request/response headers object.
- `headersDistinct`: Similar to `message.headers`, but there is no join logic and the values are always arrays of strings, even for headers received just once.
- `host`
- `hostname`: Parse the "Host" header field hostname.
- `httpVersion`: In case of server request, the HTTP version sent by the client.
- `httpVersionMajor`
- `httpVersionMinor`
- `ip`: Return the remote address, or when "trust proxy" is `true` return the upstream addr.
- `ips`: When "trust proxy" is `true`, parse the "X-Forwarded-For" ip address list.
- `method`: **Only valid for request obtained from `Server`.**
- `next`
- `originalUrl`
- `params`
- `path`: Short-hand for `url.parse(req.url).pathname`.
- `protocol`: Return the protocol string "http" or "https" when requested with TLS.
- `query`
- `rawHeaders`: The raw request/response headers list exactly as they were received.
- `rawTrailers`: The raw request/response trailer keys and values exactly as they were received.
- `readable`: Is `true` if it is safe to call `read`, which means the stream has not been destroyed or emitted `'error'` or `'end'`.
- `readableAborted`: Returns whether the stream was destroyed or errored before emitting `'end'`.
- `readableDidRead`: Returns whether `'data'` has been emitted.
- `readableEncoding`: Getter for the property `encoding` of a given `Readable` stream.
- `readableEnded`: Becomes `true` when [`'end'`](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/stream.html#event-end) event is emitted.
- `readableFlowing`: This property reflects the current state of a `Readable` stream as described in the [Three states](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/stream.html#three-states) section.
- `readableHighWaterMark`: Returns the value of `highWaterMark` passed when creating this `Readable`.
- `readableLength`: This property contains the number of bytes (or objects) in the queue ready to be read.
- `readableObjectMode`: Getter for the property `objectMode` of a given `Readable` stream.
- `res`: After middleware.init executed, Request will contain res and next properties See: express/lib/middleware/init.js
- `route`
- `secure`: Short-hand for:
- `signedCookies`
- `socket`: The `net.Socket` object associated with the connection.
- `stale`: Check if the request is stale, aka "Last-Modified" and / or the "ETag" for the resource has changed.
- `statusCode`: **Only valid for response obtained from `ClientRequest`.**
- `statusMessage`: **Only valid for response obtained from `ClientRequest`.**
- `subdomains`: Return subdomains as an array.
- `trailers`: The request/response trailers object.
- `trailersDistinct`: Similar to `message.trailers`, but there is no join logic and the values are always arrays of strings, even for headers received just once.
- `url`: **Only valid for request obtained from `Server`.**
- `xhr`: Check if the request was an _XMLHttpRequest_.
- `_construct(callback: (error?: Error | null) => void): void`
- `_destroy(error: Error | null, callback: (error?: Error | null) => void): void`
- `_read(size: number): void`
- `[asyncDispose](): Promise<void>`: Calls `readable.destroy()` with an `AbortError` and returns a promise that fulfills when the stream is finished.
- `[asyncIterator](): AsyncIterator<any>`
- `[captureRejectionSymbol](error: Error, event: string | symbol, args: AnyRest): void`
- `accepts(): string[]`: Check if the given `type(s)` is acceptable, returning the best match when true, otherwise `undefined`, in which case you should respond with 406 "Not Acceptable".
- `acceptsCharsets(): string[]`: Returns the first accepted charset of the specified character sets, based on the request's Accept-Charset HTTP header field.
- `acceptsEncodings(): string[]`: Returns the first accepted encoding of the specified encodings, based on the request's Accept-Encoding HTTP header field.
- `acceptsLanguages(): string[]`: Returns the first accepted language of the specified languages, based on the request's Accept-Language HTTP header field.
- `addListener(event: "close", listener: () => void): this`: Event emitter The defined events on documents including: 1. close 2. data 3. end 4. error 5. pause 6. readable 7. resume
- `asIndexedPairs(options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">): Readable`: This method returns a new stream with chunks of the underlying stream paired with a counter in the form `[index, chunk]`.
- `compose(stream: ComposeFnParam | T | Iterable<T, any, any> | AsyncIterable<T, any, any>, options?: { signal: AbortSignal }): T`
- `destroy(error?: Error): this`: Calls `destroy()` on the socket that received the `IncomingMessage`.
- `drop(limit: number, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">): Readable`: This method returns a new stream with the first *limit* chunks dropped from the start.
- `emit(event: "close"): boolean`: Synchronously calls each of the listeners registered for the event named `eventName`, in the order they were registered, passing the supplied arguments to each.
- `eventNames(): (string | symbol)[]`: Returns an array listing the events for which the emitter has registered listeners.
- `every(fn: (data: any, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">) => boolean | Promise<boolean>, options?: ArrayOptions): Promise<boolean>`: This method is similar to `Array.prototype.every` and calls *fn* on each chunk in the stream to check if all awaited return values are truthy value for *fn*.
- `filter(fn: (data: any, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">) => boolean | Promise<boolean>, options?: ArrayOptions): Readable`: This method allows filtering the stream.
- `find(fn: (data: any, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">) => data is T, options?: ArrayOptions): Promise<T | undefined>`: This method is similar to `Array.prototype.find` and calls *fn* on each chunk in the stream to find a chunk with a truthy value for *fn*.
- `flatMap(fn: (data: any, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">) => any, options?: ArrayOptions): Readable`: This method returns a new stream by applying the given callback to each chunk of the stream and then flattening the result.
- `forEach(fn: (data: any, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ArrayOptions): Promise<void>`: This method allows iterating a stream.
- `get(name: "set-cookie"): string[] | undefined`: Return request header.
- `getMaxListeners(): number`: Returns the current max listener value for the `EventEmitter` which is either set by `emitter.setMaxListeners(n)` or defaults to `EventEmitter.defaultMaxListeners`.
- `header(name: "set-cookie"): string[] | undefined`
- `is(type: string | string[]): string | false | null`: Check if the incoming request contains the "Content-Type" header field, and it contains the give mime `type`.
- `isPaused(): boolean`: The `readable.isPaused()` method returns the current operating state of the `Readable`.
- `iterator(options?: { destroyOnReturn?: boolean }): AsyncIterator<any>`: The iterator created by this method gives users the option to cancel the destruction of the stream if the `for await...of` loop is exited by `return`, `break`, or `throw`, or if the iterator should destroy the stream if the stream emitted an error during iteration.
- `listenerCount(eventName: string | symbol, listener?: Function): number`: Returns the number of listeners listening for the event named `eventName`.
- `listeners(eventName: string | symbol): Function[]`: Returns a copy of the array of listeners for the event named `eventName`.
- `map(fn: (data: any, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">) => any, options?: ArrayOptions): Readable`: This method allows mapping over the stream.
- `off(eventName: string | symbol, listener: (args: any[]) => void): this`: Alias for `emitter.removeListener()`.
- `on(event: "close", listener: () => void): this`: Adds the `listener` function to the end of the listeners array for the event named `eventName`.
- `once(event: "close", listener: () => void): this`: Adds a **one-time** `listener` function for the event named `eventName`.
- `param(name: string, defaultValue?: any): string`
- `pause(): this`: The `readable.pause()` method will cause a stream in flowing mode to stop emitting `'data'` events, switching out of flowing mode.
- `pipe(destination: T, options?: { end?: boolean }): T`
- `prependListener(event: "close", listener: () => void): this`: Adds the `listener` function to the _beginning_ of the listeners array for the event named `eventName`.
- `prependOnceListener(event: "close", listener: () => void): this`: Adds a **one-time**`listener` function for the event named `eventName` to the _beginning_ of the listeners array.
- `push(chunk: any, encoding?: BufferEncoding): boolean`
- `range(size: number, options?: Options): Ranges | Result | undefined`: Parse Range header field, capping to the given `size`.
- `rawListeners(eventName: string | symbol): Function[]`: Returns a copy of the array of listeners for the event named `eventName`, including any wrappers (such as those created by `.once()`).
- `read(size?: number): any`: The `readable.read()` method reads data out of the internal buffer and returns it.
- `reduce(fn: (previous: any, data: any, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">) => T, initial?: undefined, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">): Promise<T>`: This method calls *fn* on each chunk of the stream in order, passing it the result from the calculation on the previous element.
- `removeAllListeners(eventName?: string | symbol): this`: Removes all listeners, or those of the specified `eventName`.
- `removeListener(event: "close", listener: () => void): this`: Removes the specified `listener` from the listener array for the event named `eventName`.
- `resume(): this`: The `readable.resume()` method causes an explicitly paused `Readable` stream to resume emitting `'data'` events, switching the stream into flowing mode.
- `setEncoding(encoding: BufferEncoding): this`: The `readable.setEncoding()` method sets the character encoding for data read from the `Readable` stream.
- `setMaxListeners(n: number): this`: By default `EventEmitter`s will print a warning if more than `10` listeners are added for a particular event.
- `setTimeout(msecs: number, callback?: () => void): this`: Calls `message.socket.setTimeout(msecs, callback)`.
- `some(fn: (data: any, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">) => boolean | Promise<boolean>, options?: ArrayOptions): Promise<boolean>`: This method is similar to `Array.prototype.some` and calls *fn* on each chunk in the stream until the awaited return value is `true` (or any truthy value).
- `take(limit: number, options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">): Readable`: This method returns a new stream with the first *limit* chunks.
- `toArray(options?: Pick<ArrayOptions, "signal">): Promise<any[]>`: This method allows easily obtaining the contents of a stream.
- `unpipe(destination?: WritableStream): this`: The `readable.unpipe()` method detaches a `Writable` stream previously attached using the `pipe` method.
- `unshift(chunk: any, encoding?: BufferEncoding): void`: Passing `chunk` as `null` signals the end of the stream (EOF) and behaves the same as `readable.push(null)`, after which no more data can be written.
- `wrap(stream: ReadableStream): this`: Prior to Node.js 0.10, streams did not implement the entire `node:stream` module API as it is currently defined. (See `Compatibility` for more information.)

## @intellibrix/github

### Function githubTools

```ts
githubTools(options: GithubToolsOptions): ToolDefinition[]
```

Issue, pull-request, comment and review tools over octokit. Everything read
from GitHub is user-controlled text, so read tools are tagged
`resultTrust: 'untrusted'`; writes require approval by default.

### Type Alias GithubToolsOptions

```ts
GithubToolsOptions:
```

### Function githubWebhookHandler

```ts
githubWebhookHandler(__namedParameters: GithubWebhookOptions): RequestHandler
```

A webhook handler for GitHub deliveries. The body must be the **raw**
Buffer: HMAC verification is over the exact bytes GitHub sent, so a
JSON-parsed body cannot be verified.

Valid deliveries are re-emitted on `target.events` as `github.<event>` (and
`github.<event>.<action>` when the payload has an action) with the parsed
payload, plus a catch-all `github` event carrying `{event, action, deliveryId, payload}`.

### Type Alias GithubWebhookOptions

```ts
GithubWebhookOptions:
```

### Function githubWebhookRoute

```ts
githubWebhookRoute(options: GithubWebhookOptions): RequestHandler<ParamsDictionary, any, any, ParsedQs, Record<string, any>>[]
```

Middleware pair for `app.post(path, ...githubWebhookRoute(opts))`: `express.raw`
scoped to this route, then `githubWebhookHandler`.

With `ExpressBrick`, disable its global JSON parser (`builtinMiddleware:
{ json: false, urlencoded: true }`) or mount this route on the underlying app
before it, otherwise the body is consumed before it can be verified.

### Function signPayload

```ts
signPayload(secret: string, body: string | Buffer<ArrayBufferLike>): string
```

Computes GitHub's `X-Hub-Signature-256` value for a raw body.

### Function verifySignature

```ts
verifySignature(secret: string, body: string | Buffer<ArrayBufferLike>, header: string | undefined): boolean
```

Constant-time check of a signature header against the raw body.

### Type Alias WebhookTarget

```ts
WebhookTarget:
```

Anything with an event bus: a `Brick` or a `Structure`.

## @intellibrix/i18n

### Class I18nBrick

```ts
I18nBrick
```

Class representing an I18n (Internationalization) Brick.
It extends from the `Brick` class.

- `constructor(options: I18nBrickOptions): I18nBrick`: Creates a new I18n Brick.
- `ai`: The intelligence of the Brick instance.
- `db`: The key-value store of the Brick instance.
- `events`: The event emitter of the Brick instance.
- `i18next`: This brick's own i18next instance (never the global singleton).
- `id`: The unique identifier of the Brick instance.
- `initPromise`: Resolves once i18next has finished initializing.
- `log`: The logger used by the Brick instance.
- `name`: The name of the Brick instance.
- `structure`: The parent Structure of the Brick instance, if any.
- `t`: The translation function, bound to this brick's instance.
- `usage`: Accumulates token usage/cost across every `ask()` call on this Brick.
- `language`
- `languages`
- `programs`
- `ask(prompt: string, options?: AskOptions): Promise<AskResult>`: Runs a prompt through this Brick's `ai`, offering its programs (via `Brick.tools`) plus any tools attached via `Brick.use`.
- `deprogram(name: string): void`: Removes a program from the private map of programs by its name.
- `get(text: string): string`: Translates text using the current language.
- `keepAlive(on: boolean): void`: Toggles the keep alive flag of the Brick instance, which will prevent the Node process from exiting
- `program(program: Program): void`: Adds a program to the private map of programs.
- `run(name: string, payload: any): Promise<any>`: Runs a program by its name with a given payload.
- `schedule(task: Task): Task`: Schedules a `Task` to run on a given schedule.
- `task(name: string): Task | undefined`: Returns a `Task` by its name.
- `tools(): ToolDefinition[]`: Exposes every registered program as a `ToolDefinition`, each `execute` calling `this.run(program.name, input)`.
- `toolset(): ToolDefinition[]`: Every tool this Brick offers: its programs (via `Brick.tools`) plus anything attached via `Brick.use`.
- `unschedule(name: string): void`: Unschedules a task by its name.
- `use(toolsets: ToolDefinition[][]): this`: Attaches external tool arrays (e.g. MCP-sourced tools) to this Brick, included whenever `ask()` builds its tool list.
- `create(options?: I18nBrickOptions): Promise<I18nBrick>`: Creates a brick and waits for i18next initialization to finish.

### Interface I18nBrickOptions

```ts
I18nBrickOptions
```

Interface representing the options for the I18nBrick.
It extends from `BrickOptions`.

- `database`: The key-value store of the Brick instance.
- `debug`: A flag indicating whether to enable debug mode.
- `defaultLanguage`: The default language for the I18nBrick.
- `id`: The unique identifier of the Brick instance.
- `intelligence`: The Intelligence of the Brick instance.
- `logJSON`: A boolean indicating whether the logs should be in JSON format.
- `logLevel`: The log level of the Brick instance.
- `name`: The name of the Brick instance.
- `pinoOptions`: The options for the pino logger used by the Brick instance.
- `resources`: The resources for the I18nBrick, organized by language and translation key.
- `structure`: The parent Structure of the Brick, if any.

### Class SQLiteVectorStore

```ts
SQLiteVectorStore
```

A `VectorStore` on `node:sqlite`. `node:sqlite` has no vector extension,
so `query()` is a brute-force cosine scan over the whole table. That is fine
for small, local datasets (a CLI agent's personal memory); for anything
larger use `PgVectorStore` from `@intellibrix/sql`.

Vectors are stored as 32-bit floats.

- `constructor(options: SQLiteVectorStoreOptions): SQLiteVectorStore`
- `close(): void`: Closes the connection, unless it was passed in via `database`.
- `delete(ids: string[]): Promise<void>`
- `query(vector: number[], opts?: { topK?: number }): Promise<VectorMatch[]>`
- `upsert(records: VectorRecord[]): Promise<void>`

### Type Alias SQLiteVectorStoreOptions


## @intellibrix/sandbox

Wraps a Cloudflare Sandbox handle. `language` defaults to `python`.

### Interface CloudflareSandboxHandle

```ts
CloudflareSandboxHandle
```

The slice of a [Cloudflare Sandbox](https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/)

Cloudflare sandboxes are bound to a Worker's environment, so unlike the other

- `destroy(): Promise<void>`

### Type Alias ContainerExec

```ts
ContainerExec: (bin: string, args: string[], options?: { input?: string; signal?: AbortSignal; timeoutMs?: number }) => Promise<ContainerExecResult>
```

Runs the container CLI. The default spawns the binary directly (never through a shell);
override it to test, to run the CLI over SSH, or to log every command.

### Type Alias ContainerExecResult

```ts
ContainerExecResult:
```

The result of one container CLI invocation.

### Type Alias ContainerMount

```ts
ContainerMount:
```

A directory shared from the host into the container.

### Function containerProvider

```ts
containerProvider(options: ContainerProviderOptions): SandboxProvider
```

Runs code in a local [Podman](https://podman.io) or [Docker](https://docker.com) container, so
nothing leaves the machine and no account is needed.

Each sandbox is one long-lived container (so files persist between calls in a run), started with
no network, dropped capabilities, `no-new-privileges`, and memory, CPU and process limits. Code
is piped to the interpreter over stdin, never interpolated into a command line. A call that
exceeds `runTimeoutMs` has its processes killed; files in the workdir survive.

The container is a strong boundary, but it is on your machine: mount only what the code needs,
keep secrets out of `env`, and leave `network` at `'none'` unless the task requires more.

### Type Alias ContainerProviderOptions

```ts
ContainerProviderOptions:
```

## @intellibrix/structures

### Function assertDepth

```ts
assertDepth(depth: number, max: number): void
```

Throws `DepthExceededError` if `depth` exceeds `max`. Depth is
threaded explicitly through each hop's closure (incremented per
delegation), not tracked via a global/WeakMap side-table.

### Function asTool

```ts
asTool(brick: Brick, opts: AsToolOptions): ToolDefinition<{ prompt: string }>
```

Wraps a whole `Brick` as one opaque `ToolDefinition`: `execute` calls
`brick.ask(input.prompt)`. Additive to `brick.tools()`, which exposes
individual programs. This is for delegating an entire sub-brick as a
single "ask it something" tool, the default granularity `supervisor()`
uses for each sub-brick.

### Type Alias AsToolOptions

```ts
AsToolOptions:
```

Options for `asTool`.

### Class DepthExceededError

```ts
DepthExceededError
```

Thrown by `assertDepth` when a delegation chain exceeds its configured
`maxDepth`.

- `constructor(depth: number, max: number): DepthExceededError`
- `cause`
- `message`
- `name`
- `stack`
- `stackTraceLimit`: The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or `Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).
- `captureStackTrace(targetObject: object, constructorOpt?: Function): void`: Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns a string representing the location in the code at which `Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.
- `prepareStackTrace(err: Error, stackTraces: CallSite[]): any`

### Type Alias HandoffContinueSentinel

```ts
HandoffContinueSentinel:
```

Sentinel returned by a `'continue'`-mode handoff tool, recognized by
`loop.ts`'s opt-in handoff hook to swap `system`/`tools` mid-run without
terminating the current turn.

### Type Alias HandoffOptions

### Function handoffTool

```ts
handoffTool(opts: HandoffOptions): ToolDefinition<{ reason?: string }, string | HandoffContinueSentinel>
```

A `ToolDefinition` transferring control to another brick. Two modes: see
`HandoffOptions.mode`.

### Function parallel

```ts
parallel(steps: PipelineStep[]): { run: any }
```

Fans the same input to every step via `Promise.all`, mirroring `loop.ts`'s
own parallel tool-dispatch pattern.

### Type Alias PipelineStep

```ts
PipelineStep: Brick | [Brick, Program]
```

A pipeline step: either a `Brick` (invoked via `ask()`, receiving/producing
a string) or a `Program` (invoked via its owning brick's `run()`, passed
as a `[brick, program]` tuple so `pipeline.ts` doesn't need its own
dispatch mechanism).

### Function router

```ts
router(opts: RouterOptions): { ask: any }
```

Classifies a prompt into one of `routes` via a single
`Intelligence.object()` structured-output call (one model step, no loop),
then dispatches to the matched brick's `ask()`. Falls back to `fallback`
(if provided) when the classifier picks an unknown route; throws
otherwise. No depth limit at this layer; a routed-to brick that is itself
a `supervisor()` enforces its own limit.

### Type Alias RouterOptions

```ts
RouterOptions:
```

Options for `router`.

### Function sequential

```ts
sequential(steps: PipelineStep[]): { run: any }
```

Chains each step's output into the next step's input.

### Type Alias StructureHopEvent

```ts
StructureHopEvent:
```

Emitted by supervisor/router/handoff/pipeline at each delegation point.
Combined with each Brick's own bubbled `RunEvent`s (annotated with
`brickName`), a full multi-agent call graph for a given `runId` can be
reconstructed purely from the event stream.

### Type Alias StructuresEvent

```ts
StructuresEvent: RunEvent | StructureHopEvent
```

### Type Alias StructuresEventHandler

```ts
StructuresEventHandler: (event: StructuresEvent) => void
```

### Function supervisor

```ts
supervisor(opts: SupervisorOptions): { ask: any }
```

Wires the parent `supervisor` Intelligence's tool list to the given
`bricks`, each wrapped (by default) as a single opaque tool via
`asTool`, so nested delegation happens through the existing
agent-loop tool-dispatch machinery, with no new execution engine. Depth is
threaded explicitly through the closure, incremented per hop and checked
against `maxDepth` (default 3).

### Type Alias SupervisorOptions

```ts
SupervisorOptions:
```

Options for `supervisor`.

### Type Alias SupervisorResult

```ts
SupervisorResult:
```

The result of asking a `supervisor()`.

## @intellibrix/terminal

### Function chatRepl

```ts
chatRepl(brick: Brick & ReplIO, opts: ChatReplOptions): Promise<void>
```

Runs an interactive chat loop: read a line with the brick's own `input()`,
send it through `brick.ask()`, print the reply. Errors from `ask()` are
printed and the loop continues. Resolves when an exit command is entered,
the user presses Ctrl+C at the prompt or stdin closes (`InputClosedError`), or `opts.signal` aborts.
Ctrl+C while a reply is being generated cancels just that turn.

Uses the brick's `terminal-kit` input rather than `node:readline`, so two
libraries never fight over stdin raw mode.

### Interface ChatReplOptions

```ts
ChatReplOptions
```

- `exitCommands`: Inputs (case-insensitive) that end the session.
- `hint`: Shown once when the session starts.
- `prompt`: Prompt shown before each input.
- `signal`: Aborts the session, including an in-flight `ask()`.
- `threadId`: Thread id passed to `ask()`, so a configured `memory` carries the conversation.

### Class default

```ts
default
```

Class representing a Terminal Brick.
It extends from the `intellibrix!Brick` class.

It uses the [TerminalKit](https://github.com/cronvel/terminal-kit) library to interact with the terminal.

- `constructor(options: BrickOptions): default`: Creates a new Terminal Brick.
- `ai`: The intelligence of the Brick instance.
- `db`: The key-value store of the Brick instance.
- `events`: The event emitter of the Brick instance.
- `id`: The unique identifier of the Brick instance.
- `kit`: The TerminalKit module.
- `log`: The logger used by the Brick instance.
- `name`: The name of the Brick instance.
- `structure`: The parent Structure of the Brick instance, if any.
- `terminal`: The TerminalKit terminal instance.
- `usage`: Accumulates token usage/cost across every `ask()` call on this Brick.
- `programs`
- `ask(prompt: string, options?: AskOptions): Promise<AskResult>`: Runs a prompt through this Brick's `ai`, offering its programs (via `Brick.tools`) plus any tools attached via `Brick.use`.
- `deprogram(name: string): void`: Removes a program from the private map of programs by its name.
- `input(inputOptions: InputFieldOptions): Promise<string>`: Prompts the user for input in the terminal.
- `keepAlive(on: boolean): void`: Toggles the keep alive flag of the Brick instance, which will prevent the Node process from exiting
- `onInterrupt(handler: () => void): () => void`: Calls `handler` whenever the user presses Ctrl+C.
- `print(text: string): void`: Prints some text to the terminal.
- `printDebug(text: string): void`: Prints a debug message to the terminal in cyan color.
- `printError(text: string): void`: Prints an error message to the terminal in red color.
- `printInfo(text: string): void`: Prints an info message to the terminal in blue color.
- `printLine(text: string): void`: Prints a line of text to the terminal.
- `printSuccess(text: string): void`: Prints a success message to the terminal in green color.
- `printWarning(text: string): void`: Prints a warning message to the terminal in yellow color.
- `program(program: Program): void`: Adds a program to the private map of programs.
- `release(): void`: Stops grabbing the terminal's input, restoring normal Ctrl+C handling and letting the process exit.
- `run(name: string, payload: any): Promise<any>`: Runs a program by its name with a given payload.
- `schedule(task: Task): Task`: Schedules a `Task` to run on a given schedule.
- `task(name: string): Task | undefined`: Returns a `Task` by its name.
- `tools(): ToolDefinition[]`: Exposes every registered program as a `ToolDefinition`, each `execute` calling `this.run(program.name, input)`.
- `toolset(): ToolDefinition[]`: Every tool this Brick offers: its programs (via `Brick.tools`) plus anything attached via `Brick.use`.
- `unschedule(name: string): void`: Unschedules a task by its name.
- `use(toolsets: ToolDefinition[][]): this`: Attaches external tool arrays (e.g. MCP-sourced tools) to this Brick, included whenever `ask()` builds its tool list.

### Class InputClosedError

```ts
InputClosedError
```

Thrown by `TerminalBrick.input` when stdin closes or the user presses Ctrl+C before input is entered.

- `constructor(): InputClosedError`
- `cause`
- `message`
- `name`
- `stack`
- `stackTraceLimit`: The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or `Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).
- `captureStackTrace(targetObject: object, constructorOpt?: Function): void`: Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns a string representing the location in the code at which `Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.
- `prepareStackTrace(err: Error, stackTraces: CallSite[]): any`

### Interface ReplIO

```ts
ReplIO
```

The slice of `TerminalBrick` that `chatRepl` needs.

- `input(): Promise<string>`
- `onInterrupt(handler: () => void): () => void`: Subscribes to Ctrl+C, returning an unsubscribe.
- `print(text: string): void`
- `printError(text: string): void`
- `printLine(text: string): void`
- `release(): void`: Called when the session ends, to give the terminal back.

## @intellibrix/workspace

### Class FileTracker

```ts
FileTracker
```

Remembers what the model last saw of each file, so a write can be refused when the file has
changed since (another process, a formatter, the user) or was never read. Share one tracker
between `workspaceTools` and `agentTools` so `read_file`, `edit_file`, `write_file` and
`apply_patch` agree. Files are keyed by their real path; create one per session.

- `constructor(): FileTracker`
- `assertFresh(file: string, content: string | undefined, label: string): void`: Throws unless the model has seen the file's current `content`.
- `recordDelete(file: string): void`: Notes that `file` is gone.
- `recordRead(file: string, content: string): void`: Notes that the model has just read `content` from `file`.
- `recordWrite(file: string, content: string): void`: Notes that `file` now holds `content`, because the model wrote it.

### Type Alias FsToolOptions

```ts
FsToolOptions:
```

### Function fsTools

```ts
fsTools(__namedParameters: FsToolOptions): ToolDefinition[]
```

Jailed read tools (`read_file`, `list_dir`, `glob`, `grep`) and write tools (`write_file`, `edit_file`).

### Type Alias GitToolOptions

```ts
gitTools(__namedParameters: GitToolOptions): ToolDefinition[]
```

`git_status`, `git_diff`, `git_commit`, `git_branch` over simple-git, scoped to the workspace root.

### Class JailEscapeError

```ts
JailEscapeError
```

Thrown when a requested path resolves outside the workspace root.

- `constructor(requested: string): JailEscapeError`
- `cause`
- `message`
- `name`
- `stack`
- `stackTraceLimit`: The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or `Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).
- `captureStackTrace(targetObject: object, constructorOpt?: Function): void`: Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns a string representing the location in the code at which `Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.
- `prepareStackTrace(err: Error, stackTraces: CallSite[]): any`

### Function readTextFile

```ts
readTextFile(file: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<{ size: number; text?: string }>
```

Reads a UTF-8 file and its size through one handle, so the size describes the text returned.
`text` is undefined, and the file is not read, when it is larger than `maxBytes`.

### Function resolveJailed

```ts
resolveJailed(root: string, requested: string): Promise<string>
```

Resolves `requested` (relative to `root`, or absolute) to an absolute path
guaranteed to lie inside `root`.

The lexical check alone is not enough: a symlink inside the root can point
outside it. So after resolving, the deepest existing ancestor is
`realpath`-ed and containment is checked again. Do not remove that step.

### Function shellTool

```ts
shellTool(options: ShellToolOptions): ToolDefinition
```

A `shell` tool that runs allowlisted binaries via `execFile`, never through
a shell, so there is no metacharacter interpolation. `command` must be a
bare name that is on the allowlist; anything containing a path separator is
rejected, so an allowlisted name cannot be satisfied by an arbitrary binary
at some path (e.g. `/tmp/x/git`).

### Type Alias ShellToolOptions

```ts
ShellToolOptions:
```

### Function withFileLock

```ts
withFileLock(file: string, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
```

Runs `fn` while holding an in-process lock on `file`, so concurrent tool calls on the same file
(the agent loop runs one step's calls in parallel) take turns instead of losing each other's
update. `file` should be a real path, as `resolveJailed` returns. This does not coordinate
between processes.

### Function withFileLocks

```ts
withFileLocks(files: string[], fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
```

Like `withFileLock` for several files at once, taken in a fixed order so callers cannot deadlock.

### Function workspaceTools

```ts
workspaceTools(options: WorkspaceToolsOptions): ToolDefinition[]
```

The full toolset for a workspace rooted at `root`. Writes, commits and shell
all require approval unless explicitly relaxed.

### Type Alias WorkspaceToolsOptions

```ts
WorkspaceToolsOptions: FsToolOptions & { git?: boolean; shell?: Omit<ShellToolOptions, "root"> }
```

### Function writeFileAtomic

```ts
writeFileAtomic(file: string, content: string, options: WriteFileAtomicOptions): Promise<void>
```

Replaces `file` with `content` so readers see the old content or the new, never a partial file:
the content goes to a temporary file in the same directory, which then takes the file's place
with a single `rename`. An existing file keeps its permissions. A crash or error leaves the
original intact and removes the temporary file.

With `expected` set, the file is re-read immediately before the swap and the write is refused if
another writer got there first. For `expected: null` the swap is exact (`link` fails if the file
exists). For existing files the check narrows the race to the instant between the re-read and
the `rename` but does not close it against another process; use `withFileLock` to
serialize writers within this one.

### Type Alias WriteFileAtomicOptions

```ts
WriteFileAtomicOptions:
```

### Class Brick

```ts
Brick
```

A Brick is the core of the framework. It encapsulates various functionality such as AI, data storage and retrieval, processing, and logging.
Many Bricks can be combined to form a `Structure`, which may be easily passed around your application.

- `constructor(options: BrickOptions): Brick`: Creates a new Brick instance.
- `ai`: The intelligence of the Brick instance.
- `db`: The key-value store of the Brick instance.
- `events`: The event emitter of the Brick instance.
- `id`: The unique identifier of the Brick instance.
- `log`: The logger used by the Brick instance.
- `name`: The name of the Brick instance.
- `structure`: The parent Structure of the Brick instance, if any.
- `usage`: Accumulates token usage/cost across every `ask()` call on this Brick.
- `programs`
- `ask(prompt: string, options: AskOptions): Promise<AskResult>`: Runs a prompt through this Brick's `ai`, offering its programs (via `Brick.tools`) plus any tools attached via `Brick.use`.
- `deprogram(name: string): void`: Removes a program from the private map of programs by its name.
- `keepAlive(on: boolean): void`: Toggles the keep alive flag of the Brick instance, which will prevent the Node process from exiting
- `program(program: Program): void`: Adds a program to the private map of programs.
- `run(name: string, payload: any): Promise<any>`: Runs a program by its name with a given payload.
- `schedule(task: Task): Task`: Schedules a `Task` to run on a given schedule.
- `task(name: string): Task | undefined`: Returns a `Task` by its name.
- `tools(): ToolDefinition[]`: Exposes every registered program as a `ToolDefinition`, each `execute` calling `this.run(program.name, input)`.
- `toolset(): ToolDefinition[]`: Every tool this Brick offers: its programs (via `Brick.tools`) plus anything attached via `Brick.use`.
- `unschedule(name: string): void`: Unschedules a task by its name.
- `use(toolsets: ToolDefinition[][]): Brick`: Attaches external tool arrays (e.g. MCP-sourced tools) to this Brick, included whenever `ask()` builds its tool list.

### Type Alias BrickOptions

```ts
BrickOptions:
```

Represents the options for creating a Brick instance.

### Interface Checkpointer

```ts
Checkpointer
```

A save/load hook a durable-execution backend can implement against.

This is deliberately a small seam, not a workflow engine: no retry or
journaling semantics, no exactly-once guarantees. A production
`Checkpointer` (backed by Temporal, Inngest, a database, etc.) is expected
to be supplied by the application, not intellibrix itself.

- `load(runId: string): Promise<CheckpointState | undefined>`
- `save(runId: string, state: CheckpointState): Promise<void>`

### Type Alias CheckpointState

```ts
CheckpointState:
```

The saveable state of an in-progress agent-loop run.

### Type Alias ContractCase

```ts
ContractCase:
```

A single named check from a store contract. Register each with your test
runner: `for (const c of cases) it(c.name, c.run)`.

### Variable jsonToolCalls

```ts
jsonToolCalls: TextToolCallParser
```

A reply that is nothing but a JSON tool call (optionally in a code fence),
e.g. `{"tool": "read_file", "args": {"path": "a.txt"}}`. The name may be under
`name`, `tool`, `tool_name` or `function`, and the input under `arguments`,
`args`, `parameters` or `input`; a JSON array holds several calls.

Not a default parser, because plain JSON is also a legitimate answer. Opt in
with `knownToolsOnly: true` so only calls to offered tools are converted:
`textToolCalls(p, { parsers: [...defaultToolCallParsers, jsonToolCalls], knownToolsOnly: true })`.

### Interface Provider

```ts
Provider
```

A model provider. Implementations perform exactly **one** model step per
`generate`/`stream` call; `runAgentLoop` in `loop.ts` owns iteration.
This is the seam `@intellibrix/ai-sdk`'s adapters implement.

- `id`
- `embed(input: string[], opts?: EmbedOptions): Promise<number[][]>`
- `generate(req: GenerateRequest): Promise<StepResult>`
- `image(prompt: string, opts?: ImageOptions): Promise<{ data?: string; url?: string }>`
- `stream(req: GenerateRequest): AsyncIterable<StreamEvent>`

### Variable pythonicToolCalls

```ts
pythonicToolCalls: TextToolCallParser
```

Pythonic calls wrapped in special tokens, as emitted by e.g. Liquid's LFM
models: `<|tool_call_start|>[read_file(path='a.txt')]<|tool_call_end|>`.

### Type Alias RecordedStep

```ts
RecordedStep:
```

One recorded `generate()` call: the (serializable) request and the result
it produced.

### Function recordProvider

```ts
recordProvider(inner: Provider, opts: { onRecord: (step: RecordedStep) => void | Promise<void> }): Provider
```

Wraps a real `Provider`, intercepting every `generate`/`stream` call
and reporting the (serialized) request/result pair to `onRecord`.
Persistence is the caller's job, so this stays filesystem-free.

### Function replayProvider

```ts
replayProvider(fixtures: RecordedStep[]): Provider
```

Plays back a fixed array of `RecordedStep`s in call order. Throws
(`replayProvider: fixtures exhausted`) when the run asks for more steps than were recorded.

```ts
resetSharedLogger(): void
```

Resets the shared logger singleton. Intended for use in tests only.

```ts
resetTracer(): void
```

### Type Alias Role

```ts
Role: "system" | "user" | "assistant" | "tool"
```

The role of a message's author.

### Function runAgentLoop

```ts
runAgentLoop(opts: LoopOptions): Promise<LoopResult>
```

Runs a single agent loop: generate -> append -> (if tool calls) execute in
parallel, gated by approval -> append results -> repeat, until the model
stops calling tools, `stopWhen` returns true, `maxSteps` is reached, or the
loop is aborted.

### Type Alias RunEvent

```ts
RunEvent: { brickName?: string; runId: string; type: "run:start" } | { brickName?: string; runId: string; steps: number; type: "run:finish" } | { model: string; runId: string; stepIndex: number; type: "model:start" } | { durationMs: number; model: string; runId: string; stepIndex: number; type: "model:finish" } | { input: unknown; runId: string; toolCallId: string; toolName: string; type: "tool:call" } | { durationMs: number; output: unknown; runId: string; toolCallId: string; toolName: string; type: "tool:result" } | { error: unknown; runId: string; toolCallId: string; toolName: string; type: "tool:error" } | { input: unknown; runId: string; toolCallId: string; toolName: string; trust?: Trust; type: "approval:requested" } | { decision: ApprovalDecision; runId: string; toolCallId: string; toolName: string; type: "approval:resolved" }
```

Structural observability events, layered onto `LoopEvent` (additive,
not a replacement, so nothing already consuming `LoopEvent`s breaks). Emitted
at the same call sites `loop.ts` already defines: around each
`Provider.generate`/`stream` call, around the existing parallel tool
dispatch, around the existing `onToolApproval` hook, and once per
`runAgentLoop()` call (and again around `brick.ask()`'s own invocation of
it, annotated with a `brickName`).

### Type Alias RunEventHandler

```ts
RunEventHandler: (event: RunEvent) => void
```

A callback invoked with each `RunEvent`, wired via `LoopOptions.onRunEvent`.

### Type Alias SerializableGenerateRequest

```ts
SerializableGenerateRequest: Omit<GenerateRequest, "abortSignal" | "tools"> & { tools?: { description: string; name: string }[] }
```

`GenerateRequest` minus non-serializable fields (`abortSignal`, and tool
`execute`/`needsApproval` functions; tools are reduced to their
name/description/schema).

### Type Alias Span

```ts
Span:
```

A structural span, shaped closely enough to `@opentelemetry/api`'s `Span`
to be a drop-in for anyone bridging into a real OTel setup, but never
re-exported from that package, so `tsc` never needs `@opentelemetry/api`
installed to typecheck core.

### Type Alias Step

```ts
Step:
```

Represents a step in a program with an optional name, description and a list of actions.
To be used in a `Program`.

### Type Alias StepResult

```ts
StepResult:
```

The result of a single model step.

### Type Alias StreamEvent

```ts
StreamEvent: { text: string; type: "text-delta" } | { input: unknown; toolCallId: string; toolName: string; type: "tool-call" } | { result: StepResult; type: "finish" } | { error: unknown; type: "error" }
```

A single streamed event during a model step.

### Class Structure

```ts
Structure
```

Represents a Structure that can contain multiple `Brick`s.

- `constructor(options: StructureOptions, bricks: Brick[]): Structure`: Creates a new instance of the Structure class.
- `events`
- `id`
- `log`
- `name`
- `state`
- `usage`: Accumulates token usage/cost across every Brick added to this Structure.
- `bricks`
- `add(brick: Brick): void`: Adds a brick to the structure.
- `demolish(): void`: Removes all bricks from the structure.
- `get(id: string): Brick | undefined`: Gets a brick from the structure by its ID.
- `remove(brick: Brick): void`: Removes a brick from the structure.

### Type Alias StructureEvents

```ts
StructureEvents:
```

Typed events emitted on a `Structure`'s event bus.

### Type Alias StructureOptions

```ts
StructureOptions:
```

Represents the options for creating a Structure instance.

### Type Alias Task

```ts
Task:
```

Represents a Scheduled Task with a name, optional description, schedule, start flag, optional timezone and a method.

Tasks are powered by the [cron](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cron) package.

An object of this type can be passed to the `Brick.schedule` method.

### Function textMessage

```ts
textMessage(role: Role, text: string, trust?: Trust): Message
```

Convenience constructor for a single-text-part `Message`.

### Function textOf

```ts
textOf(message: Message): string
```

Extracts and concatenates all text parts of a `Message`.

### Type Alias TextPart

```ts
TextPart:
```

A block of text content.

### Interface TextToolCallParser

```ts
TextToolCallParser
```

Recognizes one text-based tool-call format that some models emit in place of
native tool calls.

- `markers`: Literal strings that begin a tool call.
- `name`
- `parse(text: string, accept?: (toolName: string) => boolean): { calls: ParsedToolCall[]; text: string }`: Extracts every tool call from `text`, returning them with the text that remains.

### Function textToolCalls

```ts
textToolCalls(inner: Provider, opts: TextToolCallsOptions): Provider
```

Wraps a `Provider` so models that write tool calls as plain text
(instead of using the API's native tool calling) still drive the agent loop.

Only a step that returns no native tool calls is inspected; recognized calls
are lifted out of the text into real `tool-call` parts and the step's
`finishReason` becomes `'tool-calls'`. Everything else (approvals, schema
validation, `Unknown tool` errors) then happens in `loop.ts` exactly as for
a native call. Still one model step per call.

### Type Alias TextToolCallsOptions

```ts
TextToolCallsOptions:
```

### Type Alias ToolCallPart

```ts
ToolCallPart:
```

A request from the model to call a tool.

### Type Alias ToolContext

```ts
ToolContext:
```

Context passed to a `ToolDefinition`'s `execute` function.

### Type Alias ToolDefinition

```ts
ToolDefinition:
```

A typed tool a `Provider` can be offered and the agent loop can execute.

### Type Alias ToolResultPart

```ts
ToolResultPart:
```

The result of executing a tool call.

### Function toolToJSONSchema

```ts
toolToJSONSchema(tool: ToolDefinition): Record<string, unknown>
```

Returns a tool's input as JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), using the Standard
JSON Schema interface when the schema implements it (Zod 4 does), and
falling back to a permissive object schema otherwise.

### Type Alias Tracer

```ts
Tracer:
```

A structural tracer. `startSpan` begins a span the caller must `end()`.

### Type Alias Trust

```ts
Trust: "trusted" | "untrusted"
```

Trust level of a `Part`. Defaults to `'trusted'` when omitted, so
hand-written messages need no change. Content fetched or read from outside
the process (workspace reads, GitHub data, MCP tool results, HTTP fetches)
should be tagged `'untrusted'` at the point of creation. This is the concrete
surface for indirect prompt-injection defense: `loop.ts`'s tool dispatch and
`tool.ts`'s `needsApproval` predicate both receive this status alongside a
call, so a guardrail policy can key off it.

### Type Alias Usage

```ts
Usage:
```

Token usage reported by a single model step.

### Class UsageAccumulator

```ts
UsageAccumulator
```

Accumulates token usage (and, optionally, cost) across model calls.
`runAgentLoop` owns a per-run accumulator; a `Brick` or `Structure` can
hold a long-lived one and pass `.child()` into each call so totals roll up
across calls (and across bricks, for a `Structure`).

- `constructor(priceTable: PriceTable, parent?: UsageAccumulator): UsageAccumulator`
- `totals`
- `add(usage: Usage, modelKey?: string): void`: Adds one model step's usage to the running totals (and to any parent this accumulator is a `.child()` of).
- `child(): UsageAccumulator`: Creates a new accumulator whose `.add()` calls roll up into this one, for per-call/per-brick totals that still contribute to a parent's grand total.

### Type Alias UsageTotals

```ts
UsageTotals:
```

Running totals accumulated across one or more `.add()` calls.

### Function validateToolInput

```ts
validateToolInput(tool: ToolDefinition<In, any>, input: unknown): Promise<In>
```

Validates `input` against a tool's input schema, throwing a descriptive
error if validation fails, synchronously unwrapping an async validator.

### Type Alias VectorMatch

```ts
VectorMatch: VectorRecord & { score: number }
```

A vector-similarity search result.

### Type Alias VectorRecord

```ts
VectorRecord:
```

A single entry in a `VectorStore`.

### Interface VectorStore

```ts
VectorStore
```

A provider-agnostic vector store for semantic search / retrieval.

- `delete(ids: string[]): Promise<void>`
- `query(vector: number[], opts?: { topK?: number }): Promise<VectorMatch[]>`
- `upsert(records: VectorRecord[]): Promise<void>`

### Function vectorStoreContract

```ts
vectorStoreContract(make: Factory<VectorStore>, opts: { dimensions?: number }): ContractCase[]
```

Behavior every `VectorStore` implementation must share. `dimensions`
is the vector length the store under test was constructed for (default 3).

### Function withSpan

```ts
withSpan(name: string, fn: (span: Span) => Promise<T>, tracer: Tracer): Promise<T>
```

Runs `fn` inside a span named `name`, recording any thrown exception and
always ending the span. Test-only escape hatch: pass a `tracer` to avoid
the memoized global.

### Variable xmlToolCalls

```ts
xmlToolCalls: TextToolCallParser
```

Function/parameter tags inside `<tool_call>`, as emitted by Qwen3-Coder and
similar models:
`<tool_call><function=read_file><parameter=path>a.txt</parameter></function></tool_call>`.
Parameter values stay strings unless they are JSON objects, arrays, booleans or null.
